title: 去吃饭
topicEn: Going to a restaurant with family

explanations.1: The subject of the sentence, meaning 'I'.
explanations.2: Indicates that the speaker and mother go together.
explanations.3: A direction word meaning 'inside', indicating a location.
explanations.4: A question word used to ask about the food.
explanations.5: Plural pronoun referring to the speaker and mother.
explanations.6: A question word asking about the place to eat.
explanations.7: Dynamic particle indicating completion of the action 'ordered'.
explanations.8: Number specifying the quantity of dumplings.
explanations.9: Measure word used for counting dumplings.
explanations.10: Adverb meaning 'also', adding another item to the order.
explanations.11: Number indicating a single cup of tea.
explanations.12: Measure word for beverages, used with 'tea'.
explanations.13: Demonstrative pronoun referring to the dumplings.
explanations.15: Adverb indicating that the father came as well.
explanations.16: Structural particle showing possession (his left side).
explanations.17: Time adverb indicating an ongoing action 'are eating'.
explanations.18: Optative verb expressing ability to eat more.
explanations.19: Frequency adverb meaning 'again', wanting to eat one more.
explanations.20: Negative adverb used to prohibit further eating.

translation: Today at noon, my mom and I went to a restaurant for lunch. Mom asked: 'What do you want to eat?' I said: 'I want to eat dumplings.' Mom also asked: 'Where shall we go to eat?' I said: 'Go to that restaurant.' We ordered ten dumplings. Mom also ordered a cup of tea. These dumplings are very delicious. Dad also came after work. He sat to my left. We are eating together. I can eat one more. Mom said: 'Don't eat anymore, let's go home.' On the way home, the weather was cold, but I was very happy.
